name: Tardigrade
description: Cryptobiosis suspends all metabolic processes to endure vacuum, 1000x lethal radiation, -272C to 150C, and 6x ocean floor pressure. TDP proteins form protective glass matrices. Horizontal gene transfer provides DNA repair mechanisms.

core_attributes.neurology: simplified ganglionic chain with cryptobiotic shutdown
core_attributes.pattern: cryptobiosis, protein glass shielding, extreme DNA repair, metabolic suspension

scope.definition: Survival fraction of tardigrade populations after complete desiccation (>98% water loss) and rehydration — measured as percentage of animals resuming locomotion within 24 hours of rehydration.

evidence.source: Crowe (1975) 'The physiology of cryptobiosis in tardigrades', Memorie dell'Istituto Italiano di Idrobiologia 32:37-59; Jönsson (2001) 'The nature of progress in our understanding of tardigrade biology', Zoologischer Anzeiger.
cross_domain_examples: Ramazzottius varieornatus: 0.98 survival after complete desiccation for 30 years, rehydrated 2016
baker's yeast trehalose-based desiccation tolerance: 0.85 survival — same molecular mechanism
resurrection plant (Myrothamnus flabellifolius): 0.94 rehydration survival after 3 years dry
dry seed viability: analogous cryptobiotic preservation; wheat seeds viable after 2000+ years

scope.falsifiability: If rehydrated tardigrades show no locomotion or metabolism after 48 hours in >5% of trials in a well-controlled study, true cryptobiosis (metabolic suspension) is not occurring.
scope.measurement_limits: Survival rate decreases with prolonged desiccation, high radiation exposure during storage, or rapid rather than gradual desiccation. Optimal cryptobiosis requires slow water loss over hours, not minutes.

scope.definition: Proportion of tardigrades surviving acute γ-radiation dose of 5000 Gy (Gray) — a dose lethal to all known vertebrates (LD50 ~3-8 Gy for mammals) — measured by locomotion and reproduction recovery.

evidence.source: Jönsson et al. (2008) 'Tardigrades survive exposure to space in low Earth orbit', Current Biology 18:R729-R731; Horikawa et al. (2006) radiation tolerance studies.
cross_domain_examples: Milnesium tardigradum: 0.97 survival at 5000 Gy γ-radiation; D. radiodurans bacterium LD50 ~15000 Gy
vacuum UV-C radiation in space (Jönsson 2008): tardigrades survived 10 days open space exposure
Dsup (damage suppressor) protein directly shields DNA from radiation-induced strand breaks — mechanism identified 2016

scope.falsifiability: If Dsup-expressing tardigrades show radiation tolerance indistinguishable from wild-type, Dsup is not the functional radiation shield.
scope.measurement_limits: Radiation resistance decreases significantly below 5000 Gy threshold in some populations. Active (non-cryptobiotic) tardigrades show 50-70% lower radiation resistance than desiccated tuns.

scope.definition: Fractional reduction in DNA double-strand breaks per Gy of radiation in cells expressing tardigrade Dsup (Damage Suppressor) protein vs control cells under identical exposure conditions.

evidence.source: Hashimoto et al. (2016) 'Extremotolerant tardigrade genome and improved radiotolerance of human cultured cells by tardigrade-unique protein', Nature Communications 7:12808.
cross_domain_examples: human HEK293 cells expressing Dsup: 40% fewer X-ray-induced DNA breaks vs control
Dsup protein binds chromatin directly — physical shielding rather than repair enzyme
Ahsp protein in red blood cells: analogous protective protein shielding hemoglobin from oxidative damage

scope.falsifiability: If Dsup-expressing human cells show statistically identical DNA break counts to control cells after radiation, direct DNA shielding is not the mechanism.
scope.measurement_limits: Dsup effectiveness measured in cell culture, not whole organisms. Transfer to multicellular organisms requires additional modifications. Protection is dose-rate and radiation-type dependent.
